# Runtime benchmarks

gocpp against real Go and against idiomatic C++20 on the same programs (`bench/programs/`, one `.gp` file that also
runs as `.go`; `bench/cpp/` has the C++ twins of the compute kernels). Generated by `make bench` (tools/gobench);
how it measures and how the regression gate works is in [README.md](README.md). Every program's output is
compared across the implementations; a difference fails the run.

> **Noisy run.** The load average was 28.2 before and 76.7 after the run (the limit for a quiet machine is 24), and the
> machine was shared. Ratios between implementations are more reliable than the times, because the runs of the
> implementations alternate, but nothing here is authoritative: the figures for the release come from a run on a quiet machine.

## Summary

Geometric mean of the time ratios (below 1.00 means gocpp is faster). The goals of Phase 15: the CPU geometric
mean against Go at or below 1.00, and no benchmark more than 2.00 times slower than Go (marked in bold below). The
flavors: `default` is what `gocpp build` does today (-O0 -g), `O2` is GOCPP_CXXFLAGS="-O2 -g0", `release` is
`gocpp build -release` (-O2 and LTO; absent until gocpp has it). Only the optimized flavors are compared with the
optimized C++ twins.
